title: IMPROMPTU: Let's Ride Ohio - The Western Reserve Greenway
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
The Western Reserve Greenway Trail is a 47 mile paved trail that runs, through the countryside, from Ashtabula, Ohio to Warren, Ohio. [Western Reserve Greenway Trail | Ashtabula County Metroparks](https://www.ashtabulametroparks.com/westernreservegreenwaytrail)

Friday, Sep 25th-Sunday, Sep 27th
Fairfield by Marriott Inn and Suites is located within a 0.6 mile ride to the Western Reserve Greenway Trail.
2782 Sidley Ct, Austinburg, OH 44010
Free deluxe breakfast every morning.
Indoor pool Free Wi-Fi
Call to make your reservation at 440-880-5500 or click the link below:
https://www.marriott.com/en-us/hotels/yngfa-fairfield-inn-and-suites-ashtabula/overview/

Schedule:
Friday - check in to the hotel 3pm, so dressed and ready to ride at 4pm for an evening ride north on the trail (12-15 miles) into Ashtabula and the Erie Lakeshore.
[Fairfield Inn to Lake Shore Park · Ride with GPS](https://ridewithgps.com/routes/57249769?privacy_code=2flx9YrtZNv3L2YmF23QZw503AGVnpFJ)
Saturday - finish breakfast 7:30am, on our bikes at 7:45am to ride south on the Trail, half as far, as we want to ride, for the day, then turn around and ride back, stopping anywhere along the way, "that suits our fancy".
Sunday will include a short, morning road ride through the countryside, before checkout and departure.
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56832661?privacy_code=bqujKSJ0Q6RnVva5ngKKNGALNqGgoyXs&via=nwBsHNSqHFjw0sNsdckfww

Helmets are mandatory; please also plan to bring 1-2 water bottles, and basic repair kit (spare tube, tire levers, pump/CO2 inflator).

title: Root’s Old Mill Flea Market
location: Root’s Country Market and Auction, 705 Graystone Road, Manheim, PA, 17545, United States
description:
Come to Root’s Old Mill Flea Market and experience the thrill of discovering hidden treasures around every corner!
From vintage artwork and antique lamps to heirloom furniture and one-of-a-kind collectibles, you never know what you’ll find waiting for you at Root’s. 
Bring the whole family and enjoy browsing 175+ vendor stands offering a variety of antiques, collectibles, estate jewelry, household treasures, tools, decor, and so much more—indoors and outdoors. 
Interested in becoming a Flea Market vendor? Reservations are required for Tuesday market. Requests may be placed by calling (717) 898-7443 beginning at the end of market day (3pm on Tuesday) through Monday at 12 noon. Vendor spaces on Tuesday start at $20.
Saturday Flea Market spaces are first come, first served. Only $10! Vendors who participate on Saturdays receive priority placement for Tuesdays.
*Please mention if you’re bringing a trailer or large vehicle, so that we may better accommodate you.

title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

title: The Knotwork Band Concert
description:
Music, Everyone

The Knotwork Band is a trio of musicians performing Celtic folk music, both traditional and modern. The band takes its name from Celtic knotwork, an art form particular to the ancient peoples of Ireland and Scotland where cords or lines are woven into intricate patterns and highly stylized designs. Like Celtic knotwork, the talents of the individual members are interwoven to form each piece of music.The audience can expect to hear Celtic folk music from Ireland, Scotland, England, and Brittany, as well as American and World music with ties to Celtic folk music, either musically or historically. Their wide spectrum of musical styles ranges from beautiful waltzes to exciting jigs and reels. The band’s music ranges from slow and hauntingly beautiful melodies to faster-paced and energetic pieces which will get the toes tapping. Our September concert will be a memorial concert in honor of William H. Sweger. Bill was a member of the Lititz Public Library’s Board of Trustees for 12 years and during that time held the offices of Secretary, Vice President and President. He joined the Board during the exciting years that led to the construction of the current library facility. Please join us for this memorial concert in his honor.

title: Children's Chapel
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. 
After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. 
The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. 
Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.

title: The Practice of Recovery
location: Urban Well Yoga Studio, 119 North Duke Street, Lancaster, 17602, United States
description:
Tuesdays in September 15, 22 & 29 | 5:30 – 6:45 PM
Led by Sarah Shelton, Urban Well Yoga Studio Coordinator, and
The Reverend Stacey Carpenter, Associate Rector at Saint James 
The Practice of Recovery: Yoga, the 12 Steps and a Path for All is a three-week series exploring recovery, healing, and embodied practice in everyday life. This series is rooted in the wisdom of the 12 Steps, something that the co-founders of Alcoholics Anonymous believed everyone could benefit from. 
Recovery is not limited to one experience or one path. Many of us are recovering from something—alcohol or substance use, codependency, grief, stress, burnout, perfectionism, anxiety, illness, major life transitions, old patterns, or the places where we have felt disconnected from ourselves, others, our bodies, or a sense of meaning. 
Through gentle yoga, reflection, breath, and conversation, this series offers a welcoming space to explore what it means to pause, listen inward, and take the next step toward wholeness. 
Each week will focus on a different movement through the 12 Steps:
Week 1: Honesty, Hope, and Surrender
Week 2: Looking Within, Awareness, and Letting Go
Week 3: Healing, Connection, and Continuing the Journey 
Participants are welcome to attend one class or the full series. Each class can stand on its own, though attending all three will offer a fuller experience as we move through the steps together. 
No prior yoga experience, faith affiliation, or recovery background is required. This series is donation-based and open to all. For more information, Click here to email Sarah Shelton

Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

title: Diamond Rio
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $49 $59 $69 
Country music trailblazers Diamond Rio have been delivering chart-topping hits and signature harmonies for decades. Formed in the late 1980s, the band made history with their debut single “Meet in the Middle,” becoming the first country group ever to reach No. 1 with a debut release. They quickly followed with a string of hits, including “How Your Love Makes Me Feel,” “One More Day,” “Beautiful Mess,” “Unbelievable,” and “I Believe,” earning a reputation for their rich vocals and exceptional musicianship. 
With more than 6.8 million albums sold, over a billion global streams, and an impressive run of 20 Top 10 singles, Diamond Rio has remained a constant force in country music. Known for playing every note on their recordings, the band’s artistry extends beyond radio hits to acclaimed instrumental performances and genre-spanning projects, including their Grammy Award-winning Christian album, The Reason. 
A member of the Grand Ole Opry and recipient of multiple CMA, ACM, and Grammy honors, Diamond Rio continues to captivate audiences with their timeless sound and energetic live performances. Don’t miss your chance to experience one of country music’s most celebrated groups live in concert. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: America250PA: Revolution to Reconstruction: Pennsylvania and the Fight for Liberty & Equality
location: The Ware Center for the Performing Arts, 42 N. Prince Street, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Revolution to Reconstruction: Pennsylvania and the Fight for Liberty & Equality









Join LancasterHistory on October 7 as we welcome award-winning author Clint Smith for “Revolution to Reconstruction: Pennsylvania and the Fight for Liberty & Equality,” an America250PA lecture. Smith will share insights on Pennsylvania’s central role in shaping our ideals of liberty & equality from the Revolution through Reconstruction and the notion that there is no such thing as a single American story. 







Clint Smith is the author of the upcoming nonfiction book, Just Beneath the Soil (Knopf, May 2027) which explores how World War II is remembered around the world. He is also wrote the narrative nonfiction book, How the Word Is Passed: A Reckoning With the History of Slavery Across America, which was a #1 New York Times bestseller, winner of the National Book Critics Circle Award for Nonfiction, the Hillman Prize for Book Journalism, the Stowe Prize, and selected by the New York Times as one of the 10 best books of 2021. With Sonja Cherry-Paul, Smith adapted How the Word Is Passed into a bestseller for young readers (Little, Brown, 2025). He is also the author of the New York Times bestselling poetry collection Above Ground and the award-winning poetry collection Counting Descent. His writing has been published in The New Yorker, The New York Times Magazine, Poetry Magazine, The Paris Review, and elsewhere. In 2020, Smith was named a New America (Emerson Collective) Fellow, and in 2026 was named the inaugural fellow of the Sachs Foundation. Clint received his B.A. in English from Davidson College and a Ph.D. in Education from Harvard University. He is a staff writer at The Atlantic. 







The event, “Revolution to Reconstruction,” will take place on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at the Ware Center for the Performing Arts, 42 N. Prince Street in Lancaster, PA. Doors open at 5pm, followed by the lecture at 5:30pm. Tickets are free, but registration in advance is required as capacity is limited and this event is anticipated to sell out. The event will include a Q&A portion for our audience, and will not be livestreamed or recorded. 







To register, please click the link below or call 717.392.4633 to book over the phone. 




Register for October 7




Signed copies of Clint Smith’s How the Word Is Passed will be available for purchase on-site, thanks to our friends at Pocket Books Shop on Prince! Cash and card are accepted.

title: Monthly Club Meeting - “The Return of the Oystercatcher: Saving Birds to Save the Planet" w/ Scott Weidensaul
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Scott Weidensaul, author of “The Return of the Oystercatcher: Saving Birds to Save the Planet” 
At a time when the news for birds – for the planet – has rarely seemed more grim, there is reason for hope. We’ve restored faltering bird populations in the past, bringing back once nearly extinct raptors and waterfowl. And despite the odds today, all around the world, people are actually reviving bird populations, providing a roadmap for wider recovery. In his newest book, “The Return of the Oystercatcher: Saving Birds to Save the Planet,” best-selling author and researcher Scott Weidensaul shows why we should never underestimate the resiliency of birds, and why creating a world that works for birds will work for everything, including us. This is a dose of optimism we all need. 
Scott Weidensaul is the author of nearly 30 books on natural history, including the Pulitzer Prize finalist “Living on the Wind” and his the New York Times bestseller “A World on the Wing.” His latest book, “Return of the Oystercatcher,” showcases what’s working for bird conservation around the world. Weidensaul is a contributing editor for Audubon magazine, a columnist for BWD, and writes for a variety of other publications including Living Bird. He is a Fellow of the American Ornithological Society and an active field researcher, studying saw-whet owl migration for 30 years, as well as winter hummingbirds in the East, bird migration in Alaska, and the winter movements of snowy owls through Project SNOWstorm, which he co-founded. A native of Pennsylvania, he now lives in New Hampshire.

title: The Statler Experience
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $24 $34 $44 








The Statler Experience brings the timeless harmonies of The Statler Brothers back to the stage in a heartfelt celebration featuring the next generation of Statler family talent: Wilson Fairchild (Wil & Langdon Reid) and Jack and Davis Reid. 
As sons and grandsons of original Statler Brothers members, these artists carry not only the sound — but the spirit — of one of country music’s most beloved vocal groups. Audiences will hear classic hits like “Flowers on the Wall,” “Bed of Rose’s,” “Do You Remember These,” and “Elizabeth,” delivered with the rich harmonies, warmth, and authenticity that defined the original quartet. 
Beyond the music, The Statler Experience offers personal stories, humor, and behind-the-scenes memories that connect generations of fans to the heart of the Statler legacy. It’s more than a tribute — it’s a family tradition brought to life on stage. 
If you cherish classic country, tight harmonies, and songs that stand the test of time, this is an evening you won’t want to miss.

Being One Center in Lancaster County
Life can be frustrating and distressing!
Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!

The good news is, you're not alone!

We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

Donations Greatly Appreciated!

This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.

Donations to the Being One Center are greatly appreciated

description:

Join us for a fascinating, hands-on science adventure led by the experts from Lancaster County Parks!As nocturnal hunters, owls seem to intrigue people more than any other birds. Their predatory nature, unique adaptations, and phenomenal senses are fascinating. Participants will learn about our local owls, their sounds, adaptations, and preferred habitats. We will end the program with an owl pellet dissection. What to Expect:Local Species: Learn about native owl species in Pennsylvania.Adaptations: Discover how these nocturnal hunters survive and thrive.Tactile Station: Get a hands-on look at real owl feathers, talons, and skulls.Pellet Dissection: Roll up your sleeves and dissect an owl pellet to uncover what they eat!Space is limited, and pre-registration is required! title: Ghosts, Monsters, and Tales of Adventure with Uncharted Lancaster
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Are you brave enough to explore the haunted corners of Lancaster County? Join Uncharted Lancaster founder and local historian Adam Zurn for an evening of eerie legends, mysterious happenings, and true tales of the unexplained. This event promises a thrilling blend of history and the supernatural that will leave you glancing over your shoulder on the walk back to your car. From battlefields to backroads, Lancaster County’s long history hides more than a few restless spirits. In the Ghosts, Monsters, and Tales of Adventure presentation, Adam shares some of his favorite stories from his recent book of the same name. The presentation combines historical research, eyewitness accounts, and local folklore to reveal how the past still echoes through the present.Prepare to meet long-dead soldiers, vengeful spirits, and mysterious creatures that haunt the river valleys and hollow hills of the Susquehanna region. Some stories may chill your bones, while others will spark your sense of wonder at just how deep Lancaster’s legends run.

Supplies/What to Bring: Choose 5 colors - assign each color a number 1-5 and keep record of the number assigned to the color. You will need to reference this throughout the project. Ex: red - 1, blue - 2, pink - 3, etc. - this is part of the chaos fun!Hook - based on recommended size for yard being used (H/5mm, I/5.5MM typically works for most projects and yarn weight)Recommend worsted weight or light/sport wright yarn if making for babyScissorsStitch MarkersYarn NeedleSee right hand side of screen for printable PDF of materials and more information. title: Screening of The Golem: How He Came Into the World (1920 Silent Film)
description:

Adults 18+Join us for a free screening of the 1920 silent film, The Golem: How He Came Into the World. The film is part of our grant funded programming through the Yiddish Book Center. Yiddish Book CenterThe Golem: How He Came into the World (Der Golem, wie er in die Welt kam, 1920) is a German silent horror film directed by Paul Wegener (with Carl Boese) and co-written by Henrik Galeen, based on Gustav Meyrink’s 1915 novel.  It is considered a leading example of early German Expressionism and is notable for being the only surviving film in a trilogy of golem-themed works by Wegener.The movie runs 1 hour and 15 minutes. Popcorn and soda will be served.

Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.

**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public

July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

title: "where time folds:" A Community Conversation
location: The Stevens & Smith Center, 13-15 East Vine Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
“where time folds:” A Community Conversation













In celebration of National Black Poets Day, Lancaster’s Inaugural Poet Laureate Evita Colón invites the community to engage with “where time folds,” the original poem she wrote for the grand opening of the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center. Co-presented by LancasterHistory, this gathering explores the role of Black poets as storytellers, historians, interpreters, and witnesses—and the ways poetry can help us understand the places we call home. 







Through a close reading of selected stanzas, attendees will unpack the poem’s metaphors, imagery, and layered storytelling, inviting participants to consider what lies beneath the language. Together, we’ll explore how Black poetry has carried history, challenged dominant narratives, preserved memory, and imagined possibility. 







Moderated and co-facilitated by Dr. Danielle Brown, Education Chair of the Lancaster Branch of the NAACP, the conversation will ultimately bring us back to Lancaster: What does this poem reveal about where we have been, where we are now, and who we might become together? Participants will be invited to engage the poem not simply as an audience, but as neighbors, readers, and co-imaginers of the future. 







Evita Colón is an award-winning poet, creative strategist, and Lancaster City’s inaugural Poet Laureate. She is the founder of Speak to My Soul LLC, a cultural strategy and production firm that uses the arts to empower, educate, and elevate through creative strategy, immersive experiences, and the stewardship of Black stories and legacies. A member of the Recording Academy, the International FLO Poets Collective, and the Lancaster County Community Foundation’s Baldwin Fellows Cohort, Colón is the recipient of the NAACP Presidential Social Justice Award, the J.P. McCaskey Distinguished Alumni Award, and the YWCA Woman of Achievement Award. Her work has also been recognized by BET’s Black Girls Rock!, Sprite Inc., and Billboard’s Grammy Contenders campaign. Her work spans museum commissions, public art, educational initiatives, and archival storytelling, using the arts to preserve and interpret Black history for future generations. 







EVENT DETAILS & HOW TO REGISTER 



This event takes place on Saturday, October 17, 2026 from 1-3pm at the Stevens & Smith Center, 13-15 E. Vine Street in Lancaster, PA.  The event is free, but registration is appreciated. To register for the program, please the button below or call 717.392.4633.

description:
Tour local farms at harvest time
WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 21, 2026
Feed your mind and delight your palate as you visit local Lancaster County farms, learn about their unique operations and sample the fruits of their labors. John Smucker is your host for this tour, which includes a flavorful luncheon featuring fresh, locally grown foods. It’s the ultimate farm-to-fork experience! 
Includes:

Two-night stay in the historic Bird-in-Hand Village Inn & Suites
Tour of local farms and a lunch made with ingredients from our tour – see itinerary below
Daily deluxe continental breakfast for two at the Village Inn & Suites or credit at the Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe
Dinner for two at the Bird-in-Hand Family Restaurant & Smorgasbord on Tuesday or Wednesday
Welcome market basket filled with local foods
Homemade pumpkin pie from the Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe

Space is limited so reserve early. Enjoy this package for $595 (plus tax). Extend your stay for only $119 a night (plus tax). 
Call (800) 914-2473 to reserve your stay. For more information on the Village Inn & Suites, click here. Walking is required for these tours. 
Requires $200 deposit to reserve your tour (refundable up to two weeks prior to event). $119 extra night available for any room type. Taxes not included. 
Empty heading
Tour Stops:
5:30 am  Rise, Shine & Dine:  Wake up with the roosters and see cows being milked at our neighbor Aaron Lantz’s organic farm. Then savor a delicious farm-fresh breakfast with the Lantz family in their kitchen. 
7:30 am  The Time is Ripe: Take an orchard tour of Kauffman’s Fruit & Farm Market and learn how they produce their apple butter and apple cider. 
9:15 am  Goats on the Farm: Amish farmer Amos Miller at Misty Creek Goat Dairy will demonstrate how to make goat cheese. Shop in his store on the farm for goat’s milk soaps and lotions before you leave. 
11:00 am  Hydroponic Farming: At Millcreek Hydroponics, we’ll learn about the sustainable year-round growing methods for their lettuce and microgreens, and tour their greenhouse. 
12:00 pm  Grown Local Luncheon: You’ve seen where it’s grown. Now taste the farm-fresh difference. Receive a market basket of local foods after lunch. 
1:00 pm   Perfectly Pumpkin: Our last stop after lunch will be a visit to Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe. See how we make our famous pies with home-grown pumpkins and take one home. You can even try our handcrafted Pumpkin Gingersnap artisan ice cream.

title: Screening of the documentary Welcome To Yiddishland
description:
Movie & Film, Adults, Seniors

Welcome to Yiddishland offers an upbeat, witty and timely exploration of this international community of artists, who are rediscovering and revitalising Yiddish culture. Whilst being a highly entertaining Arts film, full of joyous music, and performances; it also reframes our understanding of Jewish culture and identity.The film is timely in that it breaks down the current reductionist stereotyping of Jews that allow anti-Semitic hate to fester and constructive discourse to suffocate. It probes the nuanced aspects of Jewish culture and identity to reveal the multi-layered aspects of what it means to identify as Jewish and engage in Jewish culture.Through intimate interviews and rare behind-the-scenes access to some of the world's top musicians and performers working in Yiddish, we showcase the innovative works of artists who use this ancient language as a vehicle for addressing contemporary issues such as Queer identity, the refugee crisis, war and authoritarianism.This community is not large in overall numbers but they are global, spreading from Mexico and Buenos Aires, Berlin, New York, Paris, Melbourne and more.They are having a big impact. Indeed they are driving a renaissance in Yiddish Arts and Culture.Film runs 1 hour and 35 minutes.

description:

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks.Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️June 29 - ⚔️Enemies to Lovers ⚔️July 27 - 🥰😠Grumpy/Sunshine😠🥰August 31 - 🏆Sports Romance🏆September 28 - 📖Academic Romance📖October 26 - 🧛Paranormal Romance🧛November 30 - 🛏️Forced Proximity🛏️December 28 - 🎁Holiday Romance🎁

title: The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Discussion, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

🌿 BEAUTY OR BANE? THE SECRET LIFE OF YOUR GARDEN 💀Vibrant lavender and mauve blossoms sway in the breeze while butterflies dip and dance above. With every rustle of foliage, delicate white buds flash in the sunlight. It’s the ultimate dream landscape—an idyllic, peaceful sanctuary designed for pure relaxation.But look closer. Hidden within this botanical paradise, unexpected danger might be lurking right in plain sight.Is that vivid red berry harmless or a hazard?What secret is that unusual violet flower stalk hiding?Could your pet's favorite sunbathing spot be surrounded by toxic greenery?Uncover the truth behind the beauty! Join speakers Cynthia Trussell, Indigo Bowser, and Kathy Vu of the Penn State Master Gardeners for The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants. In this eye-opening 45-minute presentation (followed by a Q&A session), you'll learn how to identify ordinary, uncommon, cultivated, and wild poisonous plants in your landscape-- discover what makes them tick, and master easy, practical ways to manage them safely.Keep your loved ones safe while keeping your sanctuary gorgeous. Don't miss it-- turn your garden into a true, worry-free paradise!

Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. location: Quarryville, QVL C.X. Carlson Cultural Room
description:
Discussion, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Best for adults and older interested teens. Registration is appreciated but not required if space allows.American Disasters is a six-session PowerPoint series. Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

title: Monthly Club Meeting - “In Search of 10,000, and 10,000, and 10,000 Birds”
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Peter Kaestner, legendary birder and retired diplomat 
Peter Kaestner relates his life-long quest to see 10,000 species of birds – a quest that was almost derailed on February, 2024, when another birder claimed the record just hours before Peter saw is last bird in the Philippines.  Since then, Peter has maintained his quest, ultimately observing 10,000 species in the eBird and AviList taxonomies. 
Peter is a retired U.S. diplomat and an active independent birder who has spent a lifetime sharing his passion. On February 9, 2024, he achieved his ultimate goal when he saw his 10,000th species of bird, an Orange-tufted Spiderhunter in Mindanao, the Philippines on the IOC taxonomy. On October 21, 2025, he reached 10,000 on eBird, and on November 11, 2025, he recorded his 10,000th species on the new AviList harmonized world bird list. Always a birder, Peter took his first international trip at age ten, when he visited the Bahamas with his brother and mentor Hank. As of December 2025, he has birded in 196 eBird countries and territories. He is recognized by the Guinness Book of Records for having the world’s biggest life lists eBird (10022) and AviList (10,008) and as the first person to see a representative of every bird family – a feat that he accomplished in October, 1986. The highlight of Peter’s birding career came in 1989. Just 50 kilometers east of the Colombian capital, he discovered a bird new to science, the Cundinamarca Antpitta (Grallaria kaestneri). Peter graduated from Friends School Baltimore, where he received the William S. Pike science award and all-state honors in lacrosse. He studied Biology at Cornell University, graduating in 1976. Peter served in the Peace Corps in Zaire (Democratic Republic of Congo) as a secondary-school science teacher in 1976-1978 and joined the U.S. Department of State in June, 1980. During his 36-year career as a U.S. diplomat, he helped negotiate the UN Desertification Convention and a protocol amending the 1916 Migratory Bird Convention with Canada. He represented the United States at Conferences of the Parties of the Ramsar Convention and CITES. Peter has lived in 12 different countries: India, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, USA, Colombia, Malaysia, Namibia, Guatemala, Brazil, Egypt, Afghanistan, and Germany. Peter retired in 2016 from the State Department at the rank of Minister-Counselor. Peter loves sharing his passion for birds by writing articles, leading bird walks and tours, supporting local conservation efforts, and giving illustrated lectures on birds around the world. After the Colombian Government made peace with the FARC guerilla group, Peter helped it bring economic development to rural areas by promoting bird tourism. He also worked with the American Bird Conservancy and a Colombian NGO (Fundación Camaná) to preserve critical habitat of the Cundinamarca Antpitta in the east Andes. In 2019, Peter became a part-time tour leader for Rockjumper Birding Tours, in 2021 he became a VIP for Swarovski Optik, in 2023 he was appointed ambassador of the American Bird Conservancy, and in 2024 he received the American Birding Association’s Roger Tory Peterson Lifetime Achievement Award. Peter is married to Kimberly Vreeland Kaestner, and has two grown daughters, Laurel and Katie.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Marching to Independence: Lancaster Soldiers at the Battle of Fort Lee
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

How did ordinary men from Lancaster County end up on the front lines of the American Revolution? Step back in time with living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the harrowing story of Clotz's Battalion-- part of the legendary "Flying Camp" mobile reserve.Relive the tension of November 1776 at the Battle of Fort Lee, discover the courageous stories of local soldiers fighting for a brand-new nation, and see how modern historians uncover the past to keep their legacy alive. Don't miss this immersive journey into the fight for independence!Registration is encouraged!A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Presenter Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.

Medicare Annual Open Enrollment Appointments at Quarryville LibraryLancaster County Office of Aging runs a program called PA Medi, formerly APPRISE. This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

title: Monthly Club Meeting - "Wearables for Wildlife: Behind the Scenes with the Evolution of Wildlife Telemetry Technologies"
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Club President Andy McGann 
Andy McGann grew up birding in Southcentral Pennsylvania and his early experiences ultimately led to a career in the field of Movement Ecology. His time in academia, non-profits, consulting, and ultimately to a wildlife telemetry tech company spanned a timeframe that saw the science advance from analog radio telemetry to “smart devices” with GPS, accelerometers, and global Internet connectivity. In his career, Andy combined his experiences in ornithology with his love of technology and appreciation for geography in order to help wildlife researchers and organizations around the world obtain the scientific information needed to help conserve some of the rarest birds we have left. Andy will discuss the evolution of the technology, the current state-of-the-art, and paint a picture of where we are going.

#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

title: Coffee & Crossing: Washington's Winter of 1776
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:

Grab a piping-hot mug of authentic colonial coffee and step right into the high-stakes winter of 1776! Join living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the bold strategy, hidden Lancaster County connections, and dramatic reality behind Washington’s famous crossing of the Delaware and the epic 1st Battle of Trenton. Separate fact from fiction, sip historical brews, and discover how coffee and courage helped turn the tide of the Revolutionary War!Registration is encouraged A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.

Here’s a really fun new way to wrap up your holiday gifting while getting to know some great shops in Bird-in-Hand and beyond.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Carlson Kids! Art at the Library!
location: Quarryville, QVL C.X. Carlson Cultural Room
description:
Arts & Crafts, Children, Tweens

Ages 6-12, children under 8 should have responsible caregiver present.Our main program room is named for Charles X. Carlson, the notable local artist. And what more fitting purpose than to use it to inspire a new generation of artists! Carlson Kids is a new grant-funded program that brings together a local art teacher, some aspiring teen coaches, and young future artists!  Students will do art activities in similar styles to Charlie Carlson's work, which includes watercolor, collage, cartooning, and some experimental projects. This program will be offered on one Thursday afternoon and one Saturday afternoon per month. You may register for any sessions you wish, attendance at all sessions is not mandatory. We gratefully acknowledge the C. X. Carlson Cultural Trust Fund for their generosity in providing this program to our community.

description:
Badge Workshops for Daisies through Juniors
The Lancaster Science Factory is pleased to offer an expanded menu of Girl Scout workshops designed to educate, challenge, and empower scouts while completing badge requirements. 
Workshops are 1 hour unless otherwise noted. Register a single scout or the whole troop for upcoming workshops listed below. 
  
Mechanical Engineering Badge Workshops
Our hands-on Mechanical Engineering badge workshops cover the following badges: 

Daisies Mechanical Engineering Badge 1: Board Game Design
Brownies Mechanical Engineering Badge 3: Race Car Design
Juniors Mechanical Engineering Badge 2: Balloon Car Design

Mechanical Engineering workshops will be offered on the following dates: 
Saturday, November 14, 2026
–Daisies from 12:30-1:30 pm (register here) 
–Brownies from 2-3 pm (register here) 
–Juniors from 3:30-4:30 pm (register here)

Program attendance, cancellation, and refund policy.

Cancellations (by the registrant) received less than one week prior to the workshop will be subject to a refund of 1/2 of the total registration cost for that workshop. Cancellations received prior to that shall receive a full refund.
Workshops canceled by the Lancaster Science Factory for ANY reason will be refunded fully.

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.
